sources.title: DNA methylation age of human tissues and cell types
sources.limits: Trained to predict chronological age, not health outcomes — a distinction from GrimAge, noted explicitly in the chapter.

sources.title: DNA methylation GrimAge strongly predicts lifespan and healthspan
supports: composite of methylation-based plasma-protein surrogates and smoking-exposure estimate
sources.limits: Trained on mortality data; some critics note it may partly re-derive known risk factors like smoking via a methylation proxy rather than revealing a novel causal signal.

sources.title: Methodological literature on epigenetic clocks as causal vs. proxy biomarkers
supports: Mendelian-randomization finding that clock CpG sites are not enriched for causally-relevant aging sites
first-generation clocks reflecting stochastic epigenetic noise, limited sensitivity to intervention
sources.limits: This is the core, unresolved scientific debate the chapter centers its skepticism on — genuinely live and unsettled, not a fringe critique.
